units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 12:20">Targ. Job XII, 20</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Bava Batra 173b:6">B. Bath. 173ᵇ</cite> <he>דלא יהבי ט׳ וכ׳</he> who give no reason for their decisions (judge arbitrarily).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 173b:6">Ib.</cite>, a. fr. <he>מאי ט׳</he> (abbr. <he>מ״ט</he>) what is the reason (of the law of the Mishnah)?—

<cite ref="Kiddushin 68b:7">Kidd. 68ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>דריש ט׳ דקרא</he> interprets the biblical law on its reason and accordingly modifies it, extending or limiting, e.g. (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 115a:14">B. Mets. 115ᵃ</cite>) applying the law <cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:17">Deut. XXIV, 17</cite> only to poor widows.

<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:17">Ib.</cite> <he>אלא לרבנן מאי טַעֲמֵיה</he> but according to the Rabbis (who do not interpret the law on its reason), where is the argument for it? (prob. to be read: <he>טַעֲמַיְיהוּ</he>; <cite ref="Yevamot 23a:14">Yeb. 23ᵃ</cite> <he>מנא לן</he>).
<cite ref="Berakhot 7b:27">Ber. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>מ״ט לא אתי מר וכ׳</he> why do you not come to synagogue for prayer?—
<cite ref="Berakhot 11a:1">Ib. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>קא מפרשי טַעֲמַיְיהוּ וט׳ וכ׳</he> they give their reason for their own opinion and for differing with Beth-Sh.—

<cite ref="Ketubot 83b:14">Keth. 83ᵇ</cite> <he>הלכה כר׳ … ולא מטַעֲמֵיה</he> the rule (practice) is in agreement with R. S.’s opinion, but not for the reason he had for it. Ib. 84ᵃ <he>כטעמיה וכהלכתיה</he> in agreement both with his argument and his legal opinion; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Pesachim 21b:8">Pes. 21ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ט׳ דכתב וכ׳</he> the reason (of this) is, because &c., i.e. this is so only because &c.—<he>וּלְטַעֲמֵיךְ</he> now, according to your argument (assuming it to be correct,—what then?).

senses.gloss: argument on the cause of bereavement, consolation (v. טַמָּא).
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 18a:2">M. Kat. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>למישאל ט׳ מיניה</he> (Ms. M.; second time, <he>לשיולי ביה ט׳</he>) to get his permission to argue (with him), i.e. to console him.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 113a">Snh. 113ᵃ</cite> [read:] <he>למשאל ביה ט׳</he> (or <cite ref="I00529"><he>טמא</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 7) to console him.—<he>בֵּי טַעֲמָא</he>, v. <cite ref="I00528"><he>טַמָּא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 11:8">Targ. Num. XI, 8</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Yoma 78b:9">Yoma 78ᵇ</cite> <he>ט׳ דמיתותא</he> a foretaste of death.
<cite ref="Chullin 97a:5">Ḥull. 97ᵃ</cite> <he>בט׳</he> it depends on the taste (whether a mixture be forbidden), v. <cite ref="I00611">preced.</cite>
<cite ref="Chullin 97b:1">Ib.ᵇ</cite> <he>מין בשאינו מינו … בט׳</he> in case of a mixture of heterogeneous things which are permitted, we decide by the taste; a. fr.—Pl. <he>טַעֲמִין</he>.
